chapter: On the road and into brass bands
title: Father's advice and the first Mardi Gras parade with George Williams
summary: On his father's advice he took a brass band job with George Williams, his first Mardi Gras parade, which left him with blisters.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: So, at that point is when I left with those guys and they went and played with Richard's band and so forth and all that. Because I didn't want to be dressed like, you know, like so. We came back to New Orleans and we were playing with different people and different things and so forth. And like I say, around that time, 55, 56 is when I met Harold Dejon. And I took the advice of my father. My father said, what you ought to do, man? Run that French quarters and play that jazz. Jazz. You know? That's music. I said, oh yeah, yeah. Well, you know, youngster.
Was he thinking more music or more better money? Or maybe something more steady? Well, he. Stable. Than that rock and gold. I don't think.

Yeah, right. Exactly. It was a little bit more stable and all that kind of stuff. But musically, he liked all kinds of music, you know. So, but musically, the music he wanted me to go down and play in the French Quarter and so forth and so on, was the better music. You know what I'm saying? He said, that's moist. It was better. You know? I found out. It was right. Oh yeah, I found out it was right. Sure. So I did take upon his advice. And I took this gig from George Williams. George Williams had a brass band. Excuse me. And this was a course, I mean this was a Mardi Gras 1958 or 59. 50, could have been 58. And it was to, with the Jefferson City Buzzards. I just started off the town at 7 o'clock in the morning. Oh yeah. Went to Ottawa Park and down to Canal Street. And then back. That was my first parade.
First time you played in the parade?
First time I played in the Mardi Gras parade.

Mardi Gras parade. And I finally got back home that night about 9 o'clock. I had blisters on my both feet. So man, I couldn't walk for the next three days. I couldn't walk for the next three days, man. And I said, damn daddy. My daddy sent me 9 years. What the heck am I into now? But George Williams had a nice brass band. Sun Fuquay. Teddy Riley. Wilbur Tillman. Albert Warner. Emmanuel Paul.
Oh man, he had some great players. All-star lineup.
